citation: Mastropietro, Račkauskas, and Knopp (2025), Automating Object-Oriented Functional Modeling for Standardized Design in the New Space Domain
title: Automating Object-Oriented Functional Modeling for Standardized Design in the New Space Domain
venue_type: Conference/IEEE publication indicated by DOI metadata; exact venue name not stated in paper.md
modeling_scope: System-level New Space/small-satellite platform MBSE focused on reusable functional architectures, stakeholder/mission context, requirements traceability, system and logical architecture, standard baselines/functional libraries, digital thread, physical-architecture linkage, and automation. EPS/power appears as an example through electric power regulation/distribution mapping and a Provide Power capability linked to PCDU, but no detailed EPS model is presented.
mbse_language_method_tool: Tailored ARCADIA methodology in Capella, incorporating FAS concepts and object-oriented functional grouping; automation via Python4Capella, custom APIs, Capella libraries/REC-RPL, functional libraries in JSON/YAML/spreadsheets, PVMT, and Filtering Add-On. SysML/SysML v2 are discussed as standards/context rather than the implemented toolchain.
robot_platform: New Space small-satellite/satellite-platform context; satellite platform selected as System of Interest; pilot with Kongsberg NanoAvionics demonstration mission. Specific CubeSat/nanosatellite form factor not reported.
task_domain: Standardized satellite platform development and payload integration for Satellite-as-a-Service/New Space missions; service domains listed as communications, navigation, earth observation, and research and development.
interface: Functional and component interfaces/exchanges in Capella; payload-to-standard-platform interface context; Python4Capella/API interface to Capella Java model elements; bidirectional links to external sources such as Excel/JSON and potential simulation environments.
feedback: Iterative validation and refinement of generated model elements and functional libraries; bidirectional data flow allows external data/model updates. No operational closed-loop feedback is reported.
evaluation: Pilot implementation with Kongsberg NanoAvionics on a demonstration mission. The approach was evaluated across satellite platform modeling, functional library development, digital thread, and automation; validation used manual inspection, Capella built-in model validation tools, functional-library/interconnection tests, and demonstrations of bidirectional data flow and automated model-element generation.
rq_relevance: RQ1: Partial because the paper gives a general MBSE approach for small-satellite/satellite-platform functional modeling with reusable baselines and limited power/EPS examples, but does not develop a detailed EPS behavior model. RQ2: Partial because modeling is claimed to improve modularity, traceability, replicability, reuse, consistency, and integration, but these outcomes are mostly system/platform-level and not specific to EPS reliability. RQ3: Partial because the paper reports model/workflow validation and Capella validation tools, but EPS-specific verification procedures before physical development are not modeled; automated functional verification is identified as future work.
claimed_outcomes: Automated framework supports fast, consistent deployment of satellite digital models across missions.
Object-oriented functional analysis plus System-as-Code is claimed to streamline standard satellite-platform development and support broader MBSE adoption.
The approach is claimed to enhance model modularity, traceability, and replicability.
The automated workflow demonstrated integration of functional analysis, reuse of standard structures, and model-data interaction across abstraction layers.
Bidirectional data flow between Capella and external sources such as Excel and JSON was demonstrated.
Initial support for model variability is claimed through the Filtering Add-On and 150% models.
Reliability is discussed mainly as a benefit of standardization and reuse in Satellite-as-a-Service; no EPS-specific reliability improvement is demonstrated.
verification_validation_linkage: General model/workflow V&V only. Validation used manual inspection of generated Capella models, Capella built-in model validation tools, and incremental checks of functional libraries and interconnections. The paper says future work may add automated functional verification mechanisms. No EPS-specific verification, test, or IVV procedure model is reported.
key_findings: The paper proposes an object-oriented functional modeling approach for New Space satellite platforms, using functional groups derived from use cases as reusable building blocks.
The satellite platform, rather than the entire mission or company scope, is selected as the primary System of Interest to balance clarity, modularity, and future extension.
A tailored ARCADIA/Capella process incorporates FAS-style functional elements, interfaces, and connections across System Analysis and Logical Architecture layers.
Automation is implemented through Python4Capella, custom APIs, and use-case functional libraries that generate and manipulate Capella model elements.
Power/EPS is addressed only as a domain example: the paper mentions electric power regulation and distribution mapping and a Provide Power capability linked to PCDU.
The pilot implementation with Kongsberg NanoAvionics confirmed feasibility for automated generation, functional-library integration, model variability support, and bidirectional data exchange.
The paper explicitly reports maintainability and scalability limits in the custom automation layer and manually constructed functional libraries.
limitations_gaps: Initial modeling effort is higher during transition to a System-as-Code framework.
The custom automation layer is spread across multiple custom APIs and Python classes, creating maintainability concerns that require disciplined management.
Manual construction of functional libraries limits scalability and maintainability.
Functional-interface initialization from a dedicated model through scriptable APIs is described as needed to improve robustness and reduce implementation time and error.
Capella does not natively support code-model parallelism.
Automated functional verification mechanisms are left for future work.
No detailed EPS-specific model, EPS-specific outcomes, or EPS verification procedures are reported.

quality.rationale: IEEE DOI metadata and conference-paper format support venue credibility, although the exact venue name is not printed in paper.md. The paper explicitly discusses limitations, maintainability/scalability problems, and future verification work.
